blocks.text: `hexa-lang` is a self-hosted native compiler for the `.hexa` language, shipped with the `hx` package manager. There is **no LLVM anywhere in the toolchain**. The self-host backend lowers source directly through its own IR to native objects (ELF64 / Mach-O arm64) and links them with its own linker (`hexa_ld`); this native-emit path is a proven byte-identical fixpoint (`gen3 ≡ gen4`) and is the default for `--emit`. Two pieces of C still remain — see Self-host status for the honest accounting: a C-transpile **fallback delegate** still serves some full `hexa build`/`run` flows until the native end-to-end path lands, and a ~5.5k-LOC **C runtime substrate** (the libc/syscall bootstrap floor, generated from `.hexa` emitter SSOTs) is compiled and linked into every binary. This substrate is **reducible**: a 2026-06-16 falsification (`.verdicts/zeroc-breakthrough/`) showed ~50% of `runtime_core.c` is pure-algorithm code portable to `.hexa` today (a `.hexa` `hexa_fnv1a` is byte-identical to the C one), the syscall layer is `@asm`-svc eliminable, and the genuine residual is only libm transcendentals + GPU FFI — so zero-`.c` is an **open, attackable campaign**, not a policy that accepts C permanently.

Its defining feature is an embedded **atlas** — a ~4.2 MB theorem dictionary (P primitives / C constants / L laws / E errors) baked statically into the binary. Every formula-bearing function must either cite an atlas law (`@cite(L[id])`), carry an active `@verify`, or declare an explicit `@grace`; otherwise the build refuses to produce a binary (stage S8, fatal `HX8004`). Enforcement happens at the **build gate**, not at runtime — the atlas adds 0 ms of runtime cost.

The compiler runs eight ordered strict-lint stages (S0 parse → S1 resolve → S2 bind → S3 type → S4 domain → S5 units → S6 equational `@verify` → S7 proof `@prove` → S8 citation). A binary appears only when every fatal stage passes. After the gate, source is lowered HIR → MIR (SSA) → LIR and emitted per target. The compiler is self-hosting: the compiler that builds `.hexa` is itself written in `.hexa` (`self/`).
Honest accounting of where self-hosting actually stands (no overclaim — `git log` + the `.verdicts/` tree are the evidence):

blocks.title: Runtime C floor (reducible — zero-C campaign OPEN, not "irreducible")

blocks.text: `self/runtime*.c` (~23.6k LOC across `runtime.c` + `runtime_core.c` + `runtime_hi_gen.c`; the doc's older "~5.5k tier-A" figure undercounted) is generated from `*_emit.hexa` SSOTs, not authored by hand. **CORRECTION (2026-06-16):** the prior M3 verdict's claim that this floor is *irreducible* with *zero portable surface* was **FALSIFIED**. M3 reached "irreducible" by tallying M1 reason-columns on paper — it never tested whether a pure leaf actually ports, nor the `@asm`-svc syscall path the compiler's own `PLAN.md` flags as eliminable. Falsification (verdict `.verdicts/zeroc-breakthrough/F-ZEROC-M3-OVERCLAIM-FALSIFIED.txt`):

items: **Proven port** — `hexa_fnv1a` (pure uint32 XOR/mul loop) reimplemented in pure `.hexa` is **byte-identical** to the C function over 6 cases (incl. the string "no .c 완전돌파"). So "zero portable hexa leaves" is false.

**Portable surface is large** — a per-function body audit of `runtime_core.c` finds **155 of 308 top-level fns (50%) call no libc/libm/syscall** → portable to `.hexa` today, zero toolchain change. (`libc-dep:140` is mostly `malloc`/`memcpy` convenience that itself ports once a `.hexa` arena + `memcpy`-loop exist; `syscall-dep:3`; `libm/FFI-dep:10`.)

**Roadmap agrees** — `PLAN.md` L7589/L8183/L8341 mark kernel syscalls as eliminable; the compiler already emits byte-correct `svc #0x80` / x86 `syscall` (as the program's exit), and a `__fd_write_bytes` builtin exists. ⚠️ *Honest caveat:* the existing `@asm` block (`stdlib/firmware/asm.hexa`) emits a GCC `__asm__` **C** fragment for **cortex-M only** — it is a C-transpile firmware feature, NOT a native-emit syscall surface. Native zero-C therefore needs a **new** general syscall intrinsic (`@syscall(num, args…)` → `svc`/`syscall` with register marshalling); that's buildable codegen work, not a wall (Z2 in the campaign).

blocks.text: The **honest** floor is therefore NOT "all ~5.5k LOC". It reduces to (a) **libm transcendentals** (~10 fns — a policy choice for FP-codegen fragility, not a hard wall), (b) **raw syscall instruction emission** (proven; needs the `@asm`-svc general lowering wired for the runtime — designed, partial), and (c) **GPU/device FFI** (tier-C, outside the compiler's self-host scope). `ls self/*.c` empty is thus an **attackable codegen campaign**, not "unreachable by porting".

`runtime_hi_gen.c` is eliminated on the default arm64-darwin build (`ls self/*.c` 3→2) — `rt_str_*` come from a native-compiled object (the frozen `self/native/runtime_hi_native.s` seed), byte-identical + runtime-verified, self-host fixpoint preserved. x86_64-linux keeps the C path pending its codegen value-model rework. Full zero-`.c` remains multi-step (port batches + `@asm`-syscall wiring + a libm decision), much of it pod-gated — but the wall ("can't be done") is broken. Tracked:
(`RT-NATIVE.md`, 8 milestones Z0–Z5; supersedes the HEXA-BUILDFLOOR zero-C tracking).

the linux gen.c path's flaky hexat-regen is replaced by a deterministic awk un-escape of the `*_emit.hexa` SSOT (casefold/trim + trim-ends groups, CI faithful 3-job green) — a BUILD-STABILITY fix, not an `ls` reduction (gen.c stays a C build-artifact on linux).

`self/*.c` are all gitignored build artifacts (clean checkout = `ls self/*.c == ∅`); the real ls-reduction lever for linux is a **native `.s` seed** (Darwin already has `runtime_hi_native.s`; x86_64/linux lacks one). With x86_64 codegen graduated (#3431/#3432), `aprime --emit=asm --target=x86_64-linux` can bake `self/runtime_hi.hexa` into an x86_64 `.s` seed, letting `stage_resolve_runtime_a`'s `HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI` path drop the linux gen.c too — the next leg-B unit.

blocks.title: x86_64 native seed BLOCKED (2026-06-17, root cause confirmed on aiden):

blocks.text: the linux x86_64 `runtime_hi` native seed (PR #3460) fails at runtime — the x86_64 codegen's documented "raw-int model" (x86_64_linux.hexa:636-640) carries only the payload register and derives the HexaVal tag from the operand kind, so a string stored in a local is tagged TAG_INT(0); a tag-dispatching helper (hexa_len `if HX_IS_STR`) then sees tag=0 and returns 0, and every native function taking a HexaVal string argument returns empty/null (C-harness: 9/9). arm64 carries the full {tag,payload} 16-byte pair via stp/ldp, preserving the tag — which is why the arm64 darwin seed works and x86_64 does not. self-emit byte-eq (#3432) and int-only RUNG tests pass because they are tag-independent, so they never caught the runtime-ABI defect. The x86_64 native seed is therefore blocked until the x86_64 backend value-model is reworked to carry full HexaVal pairs (verdict F-LEGB-X86-SEED-TAGLOSS-ROOTCAUSE).

the x86_64 backend value-model was reworked to carry the full HexaVal {tag,payload} pair like arm64 (x86_64_linux.hexa +499L: pair ingress, per-value tag-slot, call box/unbox, rax:rdx pair return; plus two regalloc bugs the pair model exposed — rax removed from the caller-saved alloc pool, and loop-back-edge liveness extended to [0,pos]). Verified by full CI (12/12 green, not self-report): C-differential harness 9/9 (was 9/9 null), faithful-nobaseline linux-x86_64 (the previously-RED job) PASS, linux-arm64 + darwin-arm64 PASS (untouched), and selfhost-byteeq-real (whole-compiler gen3≡gen4) PASS at a new SHA. The new x86_64 ELF seed self/native/runtime_hi_x86_64.s ships with HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI=1 default, so runtime_hi_gen.c is now eliminated on x86_64-linux too (parity with darwin).

a grep audit falsified the "next rt_str group" premise — every rt_str function (index_of/substr/slice/parse_int/parse_float/…) already has a hexa-source definition in self/rt/string.hexa · stdlib/runtime/ctype.hexa · self/runtime_pure.hexa (the runtime_core.c `extern`s just reference them), so genuine C-only rt_str = 0. The real remaining ls-reduction is NOT porting more rt_str groups but **standalone #else removal**: the runtime.c/runtime_core.c `#else` (standalone) C-body fallbacks duplicate the now-native hexa-source and hold the file; making the standalone build always link the hexa-source rt_*.o lets those #else blocks be deleted (a build redesign, not a research wall).

blocks.title: Standalone-#else liveness — LIVE, honest NO-GO (2026-06-17, verdict `F-LEGB-STANDALONE-ELSE-NOGO`):

blocks.text: a captured-output liveness probe (c2) settled whether the standalone (non-`HEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB`) `#else` C-bodies are dead code.

— `tool/release_build` → `tool/stage_resolve_runtime_a:271` compiles `self/runtime.c` with `CFLAGS=-O2 -std=gnu11 -D_GNU_SOURCE -Wno-trigraphs` (NO `-DHEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB`) into `build/runtime.a`, which every CI gate funneling through `release_build` consumes (selfhost-byteeq-gate, release.yml, miscompile-zero-gate, determinism-gate). aiden measurement: the actual CI builder `CC=gcc bash tool/stage_resolve_runtime_a` produces a 551566B `runtime.a` with **33 `rt_*` DEFINED (T)** = the `#else` C-bodies (vs gate-ON: 21 DEFINED, 155 UNDEFINED/delegated). So the `#else` bodies are NOT removable dead code — deleting them would leave `build/runtime.a` with undefined `rt_*` and break the live `./hexa` link. This

("standalone = dead code, 0 real builds use it"), which surveyed only the `build_aprime`/`build_native_*` (HEXA_HAS=1) family and missed `stage_resolve_runtime_a`. Two build families coexist: aprime (HEXA_HAS=1, hexa-source delegation) and release/standalone (#else C-body, PRIMARY shipping). The `#else` is a Go/Rust-equivalent freestanding substrate (honest-keep, c9). leg-B `ls self/*.c == ∅` therefore needs ①porting the ~1190 common core fns to hexa-native (multi-session) + ②a standalone-build ABI redesign so it links hexa-source rt_*.o (HexaVal↔float wrappers per `F-LEG-B-STANDALONE-SCOPE`) — NOT a simple `#else` deletion.

blocks.title: UNLOCK-2 nanbox-constructor intrinsic — GO, already executed; no circularity (2026-06-17, verdict `F-LEGB-UNLOCK2-NANBOX-FEASIBILITY`):

blocks.text: the census category-(1) functions (`hexa_int/float/bool/void`, `hexa_bits_to_float`) are 16-byte tagged-union constructors (`{.tag=TAG_*, .payload}`). A bounded feasibility probe asked whether expressing them in `.hexa` via an `@tag`-style intrinsic creates a bootstrap circularity (the intrinsic needing the constructor it defines).

— the landed `__hx_tag`/`__hx_payload_*` intrinsics (CHANGELOG "UNLOCK-2 DONE") lower **directly to register `movz`/`mov`/`ldp` writes with zero `bl` (no runtime call)**; `arm64_darwin.hexa::_hv_load` (1090) already inlines every constructor (`const_int → movz lo,#0(TAG_INT)+hi`, `const_bool → movz #2`, `const_void → #4`, `const_float → #1`). The intrinsic IS the constructor body inlined; it bottoms out in the register file + immediate-move opcode, not a HexaVal call — so the recursion never closes. Verified by 3/3 aprime byte-identical fixpoint preservation. This is GO-class (the nanbox constructor is NOT part of the irreducible floor), and unblocks the Z2c dispatch core (`hexa_type_of` = `switch on __hx_tag`). Scope: 6 runtime_core.c fns + ~6 STMT_CALL codegen cases, all arm64-DONE; the only parity gap is the x86_64 backend, which carries the full {tag,payload} pair model (#3462) but has **zero `__hx_*` leaf intrinsics** (measured `grep -c __hx_ x86_64_linux.hexa` = 0) — a bounded single-file mirror. blocks.title: forge GPU GEMM → cuBLAS independence (`-lcublas` removal)

blocks.text: Goal: ship the forge cuda runtime with NO `-lcublas` link (full GPU GEMM self-sufficiency). Production GEMM cuBLAS calls were taken 7→0 by own-kernel default-ON (#3718 FP64 · #3727/#3734 TF32, `self/cuda/runtime_cuda_emit.hexa`), but the link flag + opt-out fallbacks remain. Census (r1, read-only): 12 cuBLAS touchpoints.

items: ✅ FP64 GEMM (single/batched/tn/outer) — own `_hx_k_gemm` default-ON, bit-identical to cublasDgemm (sm_120 has no FP64 tensorcore → cuBLAS also SIMT), 1.1~3.1× faster. cuBLAS-free on default path.

🔬 TF32 GEMM — own `mma.sync` opt-in default within HEXA_TF32_FASTMODE; perf parity is its own OPEN frontier (see next subsection). Blocks `-lcublas` removal because the HEXA_TF32_OWN=0 escape-hatch still references cublasGemmEx.

🔬 BF16 GEMM — own kernel `owngemm_sm120_bf16.cu` (mma.sync.m16n8k16) WIRED to production (r2, `HEXA_BF16_OWN` gate), own==cuBLAS rel-RMS 0 but 3.1-7.1× slower (per-call 3×cudaMalloc + 3 cast kernels = dispatch overhead). Research (cited: PTX f32-accum · ggml · CUTLASS · WingEdge) confirms ≥0.85× ACHIEVABLE (WingEdge mma.sync HGEMM reaches sm_120 cuBLAS parity; cuBLAS uses same mma.sync HMMA, no exclusive instr). BF16 r3 GPU IN PROGRESS: L1 direct-bf16-mma + L2 epilogue-fused downcast + L3 process-lifetime scratch (kill the 3×malloc/3 cast overhead) → if ≥0.85× → default-able → cuBLAS-call 2→0. Split-K NOT used (breaks byte-determinism).
🧱 packed_gemv FP32 — no own kernel (cublasDgemv fallback for fp32/bf16 dtype slices). FP64 packed_gemv own-kernel ships.

📦 `-lcublas` removal — blocked by: (a) BF16 production wiring, (b) own FP32 packed-gemv, (c) policy: HEXA_OWN_GEMM=0/HEXA_TF32_OWN=0 escape-hatches double as the cuBLAS correctness ORACLE; dropping them (must `#ifdef` out the call-sites, not just default away — linker needs the symbols) loses the validation oracle. Decision-gated, not a measured wall.

sections.title: Language feature surface — parity census vs Go/Rust

blocks.text: Current-state census of what the .hexa language supports vs frontier languages (Go·Rust), captured 2026-06-27 by a 4-agent read-only sweep of compiler/ + self/ + stdlib/. This node is the SSOT index of language-level gaps (NOT a roadmap — actionable items live on the ING board; history in CHANGELOG+git). The framing premise reshapes the whole table: hexa is DYNAMICALLY TYPED — types resolve at runtime via a {tag,payload} value, every fn is auto-polymorphic, and `compiler/parse/parser.hexa:1811-1818` confirms typecheck/codegen ERASE generics (Box<Int>·Box<Str> share one MIR shape) with `compiler/check/types.hexa:1-40` a typecheck stub. Roughly half the 'missing' Rust/Go features flow from that single design choice, not from incompleteness.

blocks.title: Tier-1 — true gaps (BOTH Go and Rust have it, hexa does not)

items: Static generics / monomorphization — parsed only, codegen erases (`compiler/parse/parser.hexa:1811`). Limits codegen specialization. OPT-IN slice R1 landed (PR#NN, `state/rfc_static_generics_monomorphization.md`): native `parse_fn_item` now consumes `<T>` (parity w/ struct + self/parser, byte-neutral), and a default-OFF MIR pass `compiler/optimize/monomorphize.hexa` (gated `HEXA_MONOMORPHIZE=1`, no-op unless a `$$g`-marked template exists) clones+mangles a generic template per call-site concrete type (`id$int`/`id$str`) à la rustc/zig/swift specialization. DEFAULT path stays erased + byteeq-neutral. R2 COMPLETED end-to-end emit (PR#NN): `hir_to_mir::_lower_fn` now suffixes an `@specialize` fn's MFunc name with the `$$g` template marker under `HEXA_MONOMORPHIZE=1` (mirroring the `@gpu_*`→`gpu_kind` annotation precedent), so the pass actually emits `id$int`/`id$str` instances; call-site concrete tag is captured from the const operand kind (no extra threading needed). The kept template is RENAMED to its base name as the erased fallback for `dyn` call sites (`$$g` never reaches codegen). Asserted by `tool/test_monomorphize_emit.sh` (asm grep) + `self/test_monomorphize_emit.hexa` (runtime-neutral). DEFAULT (flag-unset) asm stays byte-identical on the 3 byteeq targets.

Type alias / newtype — LANDED (native path, `state/rfc_type_alias.md`): `type Name = Underlying` (+ `pub type`, generic `type Box<T> = …`, alias chains `type Temp = Celsius`) now parses. No new keyword/token (frozen-parser safe) — `type` is detected as an `Ident` leader at item position via `compiler/parse/parser.hexa::_peek_is_type_kw`, mirroring the `extern fn` (`_peek_is_extern_kw`) idiom. The alias is carried as an `ItemKind::Let` tagged `@phase("parse_only")` + a bare `__type_alias` marker (`compiler/parse/ast.hexa::item_is_type_alias`), so NO new `ItemKind` variant → every exhaustive `match ItemKind` site is untouched. The types pass (`compiler/check/types.hexa::_types_register_aliases` → `_types_lower_type_ref`) builds an alias→underlying substitution table up front so `Celsius` lowers to `f64` everywhere a TypeRef is resolved (Rust `type Kilometers = i32` / Go alias semantics, bounded 16-hop chain resolution defuses `type A = A` cycles); `lower/ast_to_hir.hexa` drops the carrier so it emits nothing. Purely additive — alias-free programs are byte-identical on the 3 byteeq targets (the substitution table is empty → `_types_resolve_alias_name` returns its input unchanged). Tests `compiler/parse/parser_test.hexa::case_type_alias` (alias_count=4, 0 diags, fn-signature use type-checks clean). R2 gap: true `newtype` nominal distinction (a distinct type that is NOT interchangeable with its base, e.g. Rust tuple-struct `struct Meters(f64)`) — the current `type` is a transparent alias only.
Interface/trait dispatch — `impl T For X` PARSES (`self/parser.hexa:2603`) but no checking, no vtable. Method dispatch on structs works; trait-bounded polymorphism does not.

Operator overloading — fixed 21-operator set (`compiler/lex/tokens.hexa:58-73`), no magic methods. OPT-IN slice landed (PR#NN, `state/rfc_operator_overload.md`): default-OFF `HEXA_OP_OVERLOAD=1` makes the C-transpile codegen (`self/codegen.hexa`) lower `a + b` to a struct's `__add` impl method (à la Rust `std::ops::Add::add` / Swift `static func +`), via runtime `hexa_is_type` dispatch reusing the P2-6 method-call mechanism — NO new keyword, NO new @attr (frozen-parser-safe), NO runtime.c edit. `_op_overload_prescan` registers impl methods source-order-independently; helper is never consulted with the flag OFF so DEFAULT 3-target byteeq is byte-identical. Slice scope = `+`→`__add` only; op→method table (`-`/`*`/`/`/`%`→`__sub`/`__mul`/`__div`/`__rem`) + native-backend parity are follow-up rounds.

OS threads / goroutines — single-threaded by DEFAULT (`stdlib/cancel.hexa:54`); async/await PARSE but run synchronously (RFC-022). The pthread spawn/join+condvar-channel runtime (`self/native/thread.c`) routes through `hxlcl_pthread_*` shims. OPT-IN real OS threads LANDED: the shims are gated in `self/runtime_emit_full.hexa` — `#if defined(HEXA_THREADS)` maps them 1:1 onto POSIX `pthread_create`/`pthread_join`/mutex/cond; the `#else` branch is the byte-identical synchronous fallback (default). `thread_spawn`/`thread_join` fn-globals become real OS threads under `-DHEXA_THREADS`; default preprocesses out → byteeq unaffected. hexa wrappers in `stdlib/thread_real.hexa`, oracle `self/test_real_spawn.hexa`. SSOT: state/rfc_real_concurrency_optin.md §c.

Real mutex/atomic — by-value sim is the byte-deterministic DEFAULT (`self/atomic_ops.hexa:1-3`). OPT-IN real hardware atomics LANDED: C11/GCC `__atomic_*` seq-cst cells behind `#if defined(HEXA_THREADS)` (`self/native/thread_emit.hexa`→thread.c), hexa wrappers in `stdlib/atomic_real.hexa`. Default preprocesses out → byteeq unaffected. SSOT: state/rfc_real_concurrency_optin.md.

Regex — core LANDED (census was stale): `stdlib/regex/` had a libc POSIX-ERE bridge + a BACKTRACKING engine (`native.hexa`); PR#4046 adds the linear-time Thompson NFA (`thompson.hexa`, RE2-style, compile/match/search/find_all). R2 gap: capture extraction + backref/lookaround (NFA-impossible).

Package-manager dependency RESOLVER + registry — hx has lockfile/semver/ed25519 SCHEMA only (`stdlib/hx/lockfile.hexa`, `semver.hexa`); `hexa.toml [dependencies]` is empty, no transitive resolve, no central registry. The largest DX-canonical gap vs cargo/go-mod.

blocks.title: Tier-2 — Rust-only gaps (Go also lacks → lower priority)

items: Ownership / borrow checker — `own`/`borrow` tokens recognized (bootstrap.hexa) but NO checking; arena scope is the actual lifetime model. RESEARCH RFC `state/rfc_advanced_typesystem.md` §4.1: borrow ENFORCEMENT is vacuous under the bump-arena (nothing frees mid-scope), but an advisory-only MIR dataflow lint (default-OFF `HEXA_BORROWCK=1`, warning `HX46xx`, reusing the already-recognized `move`/`borrow` tokens) is the byteeq-safe on-ramp — reference: rustc MIR borrowck / NLL RFC 2094 / Polonius. Strict enforcement is blocked on a non-arena allocator (`HEXA_STREAM_RECLAIM` free-tree).

Lifetimes `'a` — none (arena-scope owns lifetime, `self/codegen.hexa`). RESEARCH RFC `state/rfc_advanced_typesystem.md` §4.2: lifetimes are erased before codegen in rustc ⇒ byteeq-neutral by construction; the ONLY wall is the frozen lexer (`151c52c8`) cannot read `'a` syntax. Honest ceiling = encode `outlives` relations inside annotation-arg strings (no new token/`@attr`), advisory-only.
Drop trait / RAII destructors — only `defer`/`drop` markers (codegen defer section), no auto-cleanup.

Associated types · HKT · const generics — none. RESEARCH RFC `state/rfc_advanced_typesystem.md` §4.3-4.4: associated types are gated behind trait resolution (Tier-1 gap, no slice) — RFC 0195 type-projection has nothing to resolve against; HKT is the deepest wall, needing a type system AND a kind system above it (GHC kinds; Rust itself omits HKT, approximating via GATs RFC 1598/2289). Both are measured DESIGN-SCALE ceilings under the dynamic-erasure value model, not actionable slices.

Pattern guards (`pattern if cond -> body`) — DONE (native path): parsed in `compiler/parse/parser.hexa::parse_match_expr` (reuses the `if` token, no new keyword; stored as an If-kind `match_guard` carrier — `ast.hexa::ast_is_match_guard`, no new ExprKind variant), bound in `check/bind.hexa`, lowered through `lower/ast_to_hir.hexa` (HIR `match_guard`) → `lower/hir_to_mir.hexa` (guard `STMT_BR_COND`: truthy→body, falsy→next arm; Rust semantics). Purely additive — unguarded arms byte-identical, so byteeq-neutral; self/ unused → fixpoint untouched. cite The Rust Reference §Match guards. Exhaustiveness checking — non-exhaustive enum-match WARNING (HX3006, S3, non-fatal) in `check/types.hexa::_exh_*` (Maranget 2007 single-column enum usefulness; guarded arms don't count toward coverage), opt-in `HEXA_EXHAUSTIVE=1` (default-OFF on introduction = zero diagnostic delta on the default build, release-integrity-first; promotable once corpus measured clean). Tests `self/test_match_guard.hexa` · `self/test_match_exhaustive.hexa`.
Struct-destructure patterns `Point{x,y}` — absent.
`?` error-propagation operator — absent (combinators / try-catch substitute, `self/test_result_type.hexa`).
Inline asm (`asm!`) — absent (extern fn + syscall emit exist).
Function overloading — absent ('later def ignored', codegen comment).

Per-field struct visibility — parse + checker enforcement LANDED (was struct-level `pub` only). `self/parser.hexa::parse_struct_decl` already accepted an optional `pub`/`pub(scope)` on each field but DISCARDED it; it now captures the visibility string onto a new `vis` AST slot (sibling of the proven `default_expr` slot — no new keyword/token, codegen ignores it → byteeq-neutral). `self/type_checker.hexa` records per-field visibility in a `struct_all_field_vis[]` array parallel to the existing name/type registry and, in the `Field`-access arm, flags a `private` field reached from a non-`self` receiver. OPT-IN via `HEXA_CHECK_FIELD_VIS` (default-OFF = zero diagnostic delta on every build path; `warn`/`1` → soft `[warn]`, `fatal`/`error` → hard type error), mirroring the `HEXA_EXHAUSTIVE` release-integrity-first precedent. WALL (documented follow-up `state/rfc_field_visibility.md`): the module loader flattens all module sources before parse, so no per-decl module id survives to the AST — the enforced granularity is therefore the type's own methods (`self`-access), STRICTER than Rust module / Go package privacy; true cross-module scoping needs module-provenance threaded flatten→parse→check (design-scale). blocks.text: `hexa verify` is the single canonical verification surface and the project's g5 gate:

items: **S6 equational `@verify`** (in-compiler): canonicalizes LHS/RHS (const-fold, associativity, commutativity), checks equality, then does a deterministic sample-eval counter-example search. Failures surface as `HX6001` (normalization mismatch) or `HX6002` (witness found).
**S8 citation** (in-compiler): every formula-bearing function must resolve its cited `L[id]` in `static_atlas()`, with kind match and tombstone check, else fatal `HX8004`/`HX1099`.

**`hexa atlas verify` / `reverify`** (tool-level): recomputes atlas F/P nodes and reports `MATCH`/`DRIFT`/`UNVERIFIABLE` against the recorded claim (ε tolerance); a successful verify **auto-folds** the verified atom into the atlas (`embedded.gen.hexa`) — verify is ambient, not a separate `atlas register` ceremony.

blocks.text: CI runs the same gate (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`); `hx commit`/`hx push` re-run the lint gate and stamp a `raw-all-attest` trailer so every commit is attested against the SSOT.

So: (a) omitting array/map/alloc/rt_hi seed .o = `undefined reference to rt_map_get_native / hexa_arena_alloc`; (b) linking the alloc seed WITHOUT -DHEXA_RT_ALLOC_NATIVE=1 = `multiple definition of hexa_arena_*` (both the C arena and the seed define them). Recurrences: (1) build_native_linux_x86_64 gcc line, (2) shipped v0.262.0 runtime.a missing array_core_native.o (bricked hexa run/build of every x86_64 program), (3) THIS build_hexa_cli driver+module_loader link. Fix = the canonical set + the alloc macro, the build_aprime way.

REAL root cause (#3833 misdiagnosed as pipe-buffer overflow): the runtime exec-drain (hexa_drain_bounded) has a HARD ceiling HEXA_EXEC_DRAIN_MAX_MS (default 120 s). #3833 redirected build output to a logfile so the pipe went SILENT — leaving the trailing `echo __BRC__` as the ONLY captured byte. A large `hexa build` entry running >120 s on a loaded host (aiden shared pool: install_firmware_hook ~156 s, build_precompile ~157 s — both >120 s) makes the drain hit its ceiling and fclose() the read end while /bin/sh is STILL building; the trailing echo then writes to a dead pipe -> SIGPIPE/EPIPE (`echo: write error: Broken pipe` on bash / `echo: I/O error` on dash) AND the captured output lacks `__BRC__=` -> rc defaults to 1 -> a SUCCESSFUL build is reported FAIL. Looks 'random' because which entries cross 120 s depends on host load; darwin/arm64 hosts are faster so stay under -> GREEN. hexa_exec's post-drain hexa_spawn_reap does a BLOCKING waitpid, so the child always fully completes regardless of the drain cutoff.
records.threshold: write the build rc to a FILE (`echo "$?" > rcf`), NOT down the exec pipe, then read rcf from disk — the result path no longer touches the pipe, so a drain-ceiling cutoff cannot corrupt it (host-load / dash-vs-bash / linux-vs-darwin robust). #3833 logfile-redirect kept; only rc-capture moved off the pipe.
